result.title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation
result.summary: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, yet generated object responses may remain inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics. Critical responses in embodied scenes often concentrate in local regions and specific time intervals. Inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model guided by structured interaction anticipation. In the generation backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates how the interaction will unfold, explicitly describing participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes. A response feedback adapter forms increments to object features from the difference between the object branch's outputs with predicted and zeroed local dynamics inputs. It also converts predicted displacements into positional biases for temporal attention. These two mechanisms guide object feature updates and information retrieval across frames, respectively. Through interaction anticipation and generative feedback, ReactWorld achieves an average score of 77.51 on RBench, outperforming PhysisForcing by 3.29 points with improvements in all nine categories. On EZS-Bench, it achieves a Domain score of 86.98 and an average score of 81.87.

AI.brief_summary: ReactWorld 面向具身视频生成，在生成主干特征空间中预测交互响应场（参与者角色、未来运动响应强度、局部运动变化），并通过反馈适配器把预测位移转成时序注意力的位置偏置，以引导对象特征更新与跨帧信息检索。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先预测结构化中间状态、再反馈调制生成特征与注意力」的结构可供核查是否能为 LVR 的 latent 状态注入与更新提供线索；但属视频世界模型，非直接研究 VLM 推理，预测内容是否真正被使用仍需验证。
